hook: Jonathan Ho received his PhD in computer science from UC Berkeley in 2020, advised by Pieter Abbeel, with research interests in unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning. He is the lead author of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models, written with Ajay Jain and Pieter Abbeel for NeurIPS 2020, the paper behind modern diffusion image models. His earlier work includes Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning with Stefano Ermon, Flow++, and robotics papers with John Schulman, and he later co-authored Imagen, Video Diffusion Models and Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance.

achievements.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (NeurIPS 2020)
achievements.impact: Showed that diffusion models can generate high quality images, and became the paper behind modern diffusion image models.

achievements.title: Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (NIPS 2016)
achievements.impact: With Stefano Ermon, framed imitation learning as an adversarial training problem.

achievements.title: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance (2022)
achievements.impact: With Tim Salimans, a way to steer diffusion models toward a prompt without a separate classifier.

achievements.title: Imagen and Video Diffusion Models (2022)
achievements.impact: Applied diffusion models to text-to-image and video generation.
